items.title: 14.5.1 Impact of burning fossil fuels on the atmosphere

blocks.text: The burning of fossil fuels is the primary cause of current climate change, altering the earth's ecosystems and causing human and environmental health problems. It affects the earth system in several ways, including greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution and volatile organic compounds (Figure 14.2).

blocks.caption: Effects of burning fossil fuels
rows: smog, acid rain, poor air quality

blocks.prompt: Why is fossil fuel combustion called the primary cause of current climate change?
blocks.explanation: Every tonne of coal, oil or gas burnt adds carbon dioxide that had been locked underground for millions of years to the atmosphere, along with methane and nitrous oxide; these greenhouse gases trap outgoing heat, and their steady rise since industrialisation matches the measured warming of the earth.

items: Fossil fuel burning: primary cause of climate change; greenhouse gases, air pollution and VOCs harm ecosystems and health.
